concerns.text: Task T005 (Initialize logging/quality_report headers) is listed AFTER T002c (Data Verification Hard Gate) and T002d (Synthetic Data). However, T017 (US1) explicitly depends on T005 to append exclusion counts to the initialized headers. If T002c runs before T005, the hard gate logic (which may need to log exclusion reasons if data is invalid) or subsequent US1 tasks will fail to write to a properly initialized file. T005 must precede T002c and all US tasks.

Task T021 (LME Model) is marked [P] (parallel-safe) but the description explicitly states: 'Note: This task depends on T015 (US1) completion to determine data artifact state (target_salience column presence).' A task that cannot run until a specific upstream task completes is NOT parallel-safe. The [P] tag is incorrect and misleading for the execution engine.

Task T022 (Collinearity mitigation) is listed as a separate task from T021, but the description of T021 already includes the logic for VIF calculation and dropping predictors. Splitting this logic into T022 creates a hidden dependency where T022 must run after T021's partial execution, yet T022 is marked [P] and placed in the same phase without explicit ordering constraints. This risks the LME model being fitted without collinearity checks if the tasks are executed in parallel.

Task T029 (Ground-truth labeling) is marked [P] but involves writing to `results/limitations.md` and modifying `results/classification_metrics.csv`. If T030 (Evaluation) or T031 (Sensitivity) run in parallel and also write to these files, a race condition exists. The [P] tag should be removed or the file paths must be distinct to ensure parallel safety.
